summary: Orange County, NY fire tower and cabin built 1930 near Lake Pocatello; observer-staffed; listed gone, with no removal date or site description in sources read.

facts.design: Tower with an observation platform 60 feet above the ground and a cabin at its base (1930 newspaper); overall height not stated
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by firelookout.org; no removal date or method found in the two sources read
facts.agency: New York Conservation Department erected the tower; Orange County Board of Supervisors paid half the cabin cost, a private gift the other half

events.note: Tower and cabin ready for public inspection in August 1930 at Sayer's Hill near Lake Pocatello; state report says erected on Pocatello Mountain
Observer on duty; tower open to the public when the observer was there, usually 9 to 5
More than 300 visitors in August 1930; part of a proposed plan of five towers for the district
Lake Pocatello property owners' association sought support to continue the fire tower and watchman

evidence.supports: tower and cabin at Sayer's Hill near Lake Pocatello ready in August 1930
evidence.quote: The new fire tower and cabin at Sayer's Hill near Lake Pocatello are ready for public inspection.

evidence.supports: more than 300 visitors in August; platform 60 feet above ground
evidence.quote: more than 300 persons visited the tower during August and made observations from the platform, sixty feet above the ground.

evidence.supports: view of about 40 miles from the platform
evidence.quote: Usual visibility from the observation platform include a forty mile radius

evidence.supports: county paid half the cabin cost
evidence.quote: Money for half the cost of building the cabin at the base of the tower was appropriated by Orange County Board of Supervisors

evidence.supports: private gift paid the other half of the cabin cost
evidence.quote: the other half was a gift of Robert M. (unreadable) of Chester

evidence.supports: one of a proposed five towers
evidence.quote: The tower is one of a proposed plan of five to cover the district.

evidence.supports: state report: erected on Pocatello Mountain, protects the Shawangunk range slopes
evidence.quote: This tower was erected on Pocatello Mountain, and affords needed protection to the entire eastern and southern slopes of the Shawangunk Mountain range.

evidence.supports: open to the public when the observer was on duty, 9 to 5
evidence.quote: The tower will be open to the public when the observer is there, usually from nine until five o'clock daily.

evidence.supports: 1946 association asked for support to continue the tower and watchman
evidence.quote: Association members also decided to ask Assemblyman Wilson C. Van Duzer's support for continuation of the fire tower and services of the watchman at the lake.
Twentieth Annual Report of the Conservation Department

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1930 newspaper places the tower on Sayer's Hill near Lake Pocatello; the 1930 state report says Pocatello Mountain. Likely the same site, but no source confirms it.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, neither giving a removal date or method, so the removal is undated and the site today is unknown. The 60 ft figure is the observation platform height from the 1930 newspaper, not an overall height, so height_m is left out. Access is omitted: no source read describes the site now. The name Sayer's Hill may be the same summit (not confirmed). A search for other records found nothing reliable; the NYSFFLA searchable list and Orange County historical society are the next leads.
